subject: ba
title: Documents Used by Business Organisations
objectives: Identify the legal documents required for company formation.
Distinguish between the Memorandum and Articles of Association.
Understand the strategic importance of Vision, Mission, Objectives, Strategy and Policy documents.
Analyse the roles of feasibility reports, business plans and meeting minutes.
study:
Documentation is a business's paper trail — it provides legal evidence of existence, defines operational boundaries, and communicates strategic intent to stakeholders.

Key termMemorandum of Association — the company's 'constitution,' defining its relationship with the outside world. Contains the Name, Registered Office, Objects (what the company is permitted to do), Liability and Capital clauses.

Where the Memorandum governs external relationships, the Articles of Association govern internal management — director appointments, meeting procedures, voting rights and share transfer rules — and must always be subordinate to, and consistent with, the Memorandum. A Prospectus is an invitation to the public to subscribe for a company's shares or debentures, disclosing enough financial and operational detail for investors to make an informed decision. The Certificate of Incorporation, issued in Nigeria by the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC), is effectively the company's birth certificate. A public company additionally needs a Certificate of Trading before it can commence business — a private company can start trading immediately on incorporation, but a public company cannot.

Exam tipThe Memorandum/Articles distinction is a recurring exam favourite: Memorandum = external relationship and scope of activity; Articles = internal governance rules. If a company wants to change how it runs board meetings, it amends its Articles, not its Memorandum.

Before committing resources, businesses often commission a Feasibility Report to assess a venture's market, technical, financial and managerial viability. A Business Plan then lays out a roadmap — executive summary, market analysis, organisation structure, marketing strategy, and financial projections — partly to guide the business and partly to attract funding. Minutes are the official written record of what was decided at a meeting. Supporting schedules include the Schedule of Non-Current Assets (listing machinery and buildings), the Schedule of Directors (names, addresses, occupations) and the Schedule of Shareholders.

Strategic documents sit on their own spectrum. A Vision is a description of what the organisation wants to become in the distant future ("to be the leading provider of energy in Africa"). A Mission describes the organisation's current core purpose — what it is and why it exists right now. Objectives are specific, measurable targets. Strategies are the long-term plans for achieving those objectives, operating at three levels — corporate (overall direction), business (competitive position within a market segment), and functional (how one department, like HR or finance, supports the wider strategy). Policies are the broad guidelines that link strategy to day-to-day decision-making.
recap:
• Memorandum of Association = external relationship/constitution (Name, Registered Office, Objects, Liability, Capital clauses).
  • Articles of Association = internal governance rules, subordinate to the Memorandum.
  • Prospectus = invitation to the public to buy shares/debentures.
  • Certificate of Incorporation (CAC) = birth certificate; public companies also need a Certificate of Trading before commencing business.
  • Feasibility Report = viability check; Business Plan = roadmap + funding tool; Minutes = official record of meeting decisions.
  • Vision = future aspiration; Mission = current core purpose; Objectives = specific/measurable; Strategy = long-term plan (corporate/business/functional); Policy = decision-making guideline.
